travel.intro: Most guests fly into Edmonton International (YEG). The venues are in south Edmonton, about 30 minutes from the airport.

airports.name: Edmonton International
airports.tips: Direct flights from major Canadian hubs. Connections from India typically through Toronto or Vancouver.

gettingAround.title: Rideshare and taxis
gettingAround.text: Uber and taxis are available throughout the area. Expect about [$40 to $60] from YEG to the hotels and venues.

gettingAround.title: Car rental
gettingAround.text: A rental car is recommended. The venues are a short drive apart in south Edmonton. Parking at every event is free or inexpensive.

gettingAround.title: Transit
gettingAround.text: ETS buses and the LRT do not conveniently reach every venue, so plan on a car or rideshare.

international.title: Travelling from outside Canada
international.text: Check entry requirements early. Visitors from visa-exempt countries need an eTA (about CAD $7, usually approved within minutes). Others may need a visitor visa, which can take weeks. We are happy to provide an invitation letter; message a coordinator.

faq.q: What are Mehendi, Haldi and Vidhi, and the wedding?
faq.a: Mehendi is henna at CISE. Haldi and Vidhi is the blessing at CISE. The wedding ceremony is at the Grand Imperial. Each invitation lists the events you are invited to.
The Baraat is the groom's joyful procession to the ceremony, with drums, dancing and family. It begins at 3:30 PM on the wedding day.
Yes, everyone is welcome. Wear shoes you can dance in, bring water, and follow the dhol. No experience required.

faq.q: What should I wear to each event?
faq.a: Mehendi: colourful and comfortable. Haldi and Vidhi: old yellow or white clothes you can stain. Wedding: colourful and comfortable — wear whatever you feel comfortable in. Rich, elegant colours are welcome; it is better to avoid black.

faq.q: I have never worn Indian clothes. Where can I get some?
faq.a: Message a coordinator and we will point you to shops in Edmonton, or to rentals. You are also welcome in formal Western attire.
The wedding menu is fully vegetarian, with vegan and Jain options. Please note any allergies on your RSVP.

faq.q: Do I need to cover my head at the ceremony?
faq.a: Head coverings are welcome but not required. If you would like one, we will have scarves and caps at the entrance. Please remove your shoes before entering the ceremony space.
About 90 minutes. We will have a program explaining each ritual, and seating for everyone.
Yes! Children are welcome at all events. There will be a quiet room near the ceremony.

faq.q: Do you have a registry? What about cash gifts?
faq.a: Your presence is the best gift. Cash or cheques are traditional and appreciated.
Every venue has free or inexpensive parking on site. Accessible spaces are beside each main entrance.
No shuttles are planned at this time; we recommend a rental car or rideshare.
Please arrive 15 to 20 minutes early so you can find your seat before each event begins.
